# Controlled Chatbot Interactive Runtime Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `completed`
- Updated: `2026-07-29T16:19:05Z`

## Objective

Deliver a usable published controlled-chatbot interface whose configured model, message composer, transcript, and controlled execution path work together end to end.

## Discovery

The approved typed composition/runtime bridge remains valid. The desktop currently has one BrowserWindow, one broad preload surface, and one shared SQLite database; launched visual systems are rendered in a modal. System data is only logically keyed by workspace and release inside the shared store. The requested successor therefore also needs a host-owned runtime-instance manager that opens a dedicated sandboxed system window and routes runtime data through a physical database selected for that exact installed system instance.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: The change adds a renderer-process boundary, a new IPC surface, a selected-model invocation path, and a physical per-system persistence boundary for sensitive runtime data.
- Protected assets:
  - Exact published system, runtime instance, release, and model identity
  - Protected instructions and invocation context
  - User messages, assistant transcript, and system-owned runtime records
  - Execution approval and runtime-readiness authority
  - Per-system database placement metadata, credentials, migrations, backups, and audit evidence
  - Bounded host resources and safe diagnostics
- Trust boundaries:
  - Builder renderer to desktop main-process runtime-instance manager
  - Sandboxed system renderer and least-authority preload to sender-bound IPC
  - Runtime instance to its host-selected physical database
  - Composer UI to authorized workspace model inventory
  - Published runtime controller to application conversation services
  - Application orchestration to the Python text-generation adapter
  - Persisted transcript to bounded user-visible rendering
  - Managed database provisioner to least-privilege runtime database role
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - A system renderer forges another runtime-instance, workspace, release, model, or database identity.
  - A broad preload or unvalidated IPC sender reaches builder, filesystem, credential, or another system's capabilities.
  - Navigation, window creation, browser storage, or remote content escapes the intended local system surface.
  - A database selector accepts a renderer path, display name, traversal segment, connection string, or cross-system identifier.
  - The ordinary managed runtime role provisions, owns, drops, or connects to another system database.
  - A stale release or model reference bypasses reviewed-plan, readiness, approval, or migration checks.
  - Protected prompts, provider payloads, credentials, local paths, or private transcript content leak into diagnostics or roadmap evidence.
  - Repeated sends, oversized content, unbounded transcript rendering, database pools, or open windows exhaust resources.
- Controls:
  - Create and track system windows only in the main process from a verified running launch descriptor and host-owned runtime-instance record.
  - Use a dedicated packaged renderer/preload, unique non-persistent session partition, restrictive content policy, sandbox and context isolation, no Node integration, denied navigation/new windows, and exact sender-to-instance IPC binding.
  - Derive local database locations from normalized opaque runtime-instance ids under a contained host root; never expose paths or handles to renderers.
  - Use one physical SQLite database per desktop runtime instance and a provisioner-owned dedicated PostgreSQL database plus least-privilege connection binding for managed runtime instances.
  - Keep lifecycle/build/deployment mappings in the control plane and open only the selected instance data plane after exact association, schema, health, and compatibility checks.
  - Resolve only typed workspace-authorized text-capable model records and bind their exact identity into immutable build/runtime evidence.
  - Invoke only through existing application-owned session, approval, readiness, runtime guard, protected-context, and adapter boundaries.
  - Normalize and bound input, disable duplicate submission while busy, bound transcript reads, cap active windows/connections, and sanitize failures.
  - Separate stop, uninstall, retained-data deletion, migration, backup, restore, and recovery so ordinary lifecycle actions cannot silently destroy or cross-load data.
- Verification:
  - Electron tests for sandboxed webPreferences, dedicated preload surface, partition isolation, denied navigation/window creation, and forged/destroyed/subframe sender rejection.
  - Focused database tests proving two runtime instances cannot read, write, enumerate, migrate, back up, or restore each other's records.
  - Path and connection denial tests for traversal, display-name selection, cross-workspace/runtime identifiers, stale bindings, and renderer-supplied infrastructure details.
  - Managed PostgreSQL qualification with a provisioner role separated from runtime roles and cross-database connection denial.
  - Focused denial tests for forged, stale, cross-workspace, incompatible, and unavailable model selections and source associations.
  - UI tests for editable bounded input, keyboard and button submission, busy-state duplicate suppression, empty history, accessible live transcript, and sanitized errors.
  - End-to-end packaged-desktop test proving Start opens a separate system window, a real user turn reaches the controlled adapter, and only that system database receives the persisted exchange.
  - Restart, stop, upgrade, uninstall-retention, backup/restore, and explicit-delete recovery tests with synthetic fixtures.
  - Desktop/thin transport parity and non-disclosure assertions using synthetic fixtures.
- Residual risks:
  - A BrowserWindow and separate database do not protect against a compromised Electron main process or operating-system account.
  - Model quality and prompt-injection resistance still require deployment-specific evaluation and cannot be guaranteed by UI or storage isolation.
  - Managed database provisioning, backup, recovery, and resource ceilings require controlled-environment qualification.
  - Encryption at rest and tenant-managed keys remain separate controls unless explicitly added by an approved successor decision.
  - Streaming, tools, retrieval, memory, multimodal input, cancellation, and retry remain intentionally unsupported.

### Constraints

- Keep reusable asset definitions and backing resources declarative; do not execute arbitrary asset-authored code in a trusted renderer.
- Use the existing controlled conversation application services and Python text-generation adapter as the only model invocation path.
- Store an exact authorized model-record reference selected from workspace-visible text-capable inventory; do not accept a free-form provider or model identifier.
- Open a visual published system in a dedicated Electron BrowserWindow rather than a modal in the builder window.
- Use a dedicated renderer entry and least-authority preload for system windows; keep context isolation, process sandboxing, Node integration disabled, web security enabled, navigation constrained, new-window creation denied, and IPC bound to the exact owned webContents.
- Assign an opaque host-owned runtime-instance identity to each installed system instance; renderer input, display names, release ids, and filesystem paths must not select a database.
- Keep platform control-plane records in the existing organization-aware database while placing system-owned runtime records in a physical database dedicated to the runtime instance.
- Preserve a runtime instance and its data intentionally across compatible release upgrades; stop closes active resources, and uninstall must not erase data without a separate explicit destructive action and retention policy.
- Show an empty history before the first real message and render only bounded persisted transcript entries.
- Keep tools, retrieval, memory, multimodal input, streaming, cancel, and retry outside this successor roadmap unless an existing supported path proves them end to end.
- Maintain shared application/controller behavior across desktop and managed hosts while keeping Electron windows, preloads, database provisioning, pools, and paths in host/adapters.
- Use focused tests within increments and run repository-wide gates once after each complete increment.

- [Controlled conversational execution architecture](<architecture/controlled-conversational-system-execution.md>) - Requires verified composition, reviewed execution plan, current runtime readiness, explicit session approval, bounded transcript exposure, and application-owned invocation.
- [Host model](<architecture/host-model.md>) - Makes the desktop or server host the execution authority and keeps lifecycle, runtime roots, and launch descriptors host-owned.
- [Persistence and storage architecture](<architecture/persistence-and-storage.md>) - Requires deployment-shaped adapters, adapter-owned physical locations, monotonic migrations, bounded recovery, and no infrastructure details in application contracts.
- [Current Electron bootstrap](<../apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts>) - Creates one main BrowserWindow and one shared SQLite database before composing all desktop services and IPC.
- [Current system-data repository](<../modules/adapters/persistence/system-data/createStructuredSystemDataRepository.ts>) - Stores all system records and audit entries in shared namespaces with workspace and release keys rather than a separate physical database.
- [Published runtime application](<../apps/desktop/src/system-runtime/SystemRuntimeApp.tsx>) - Renders the exact started release in the dedicated runtime window and exposes only bounded transcript read and message submission behavior.
- [Electron process model](<https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/process-model>) - Each BrowserWindow owns a renderer process while the main process owns privileged lifecycle and window management.
- [Electron security checklist](<https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/security>) - Requires context isolation, process sandboxing, no Node integration, limited navigation/window creation, restrictive content policy, and IPC sender validation.
- [Electron process sandboxing](<https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/sandbox>) - A sandboxed renderer delegates privileged work through narrowly exposed IPC and must not receive broad Node authority.
- [PostgreSQL database overview](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/manage-ag-overview.html>) - Separate databases provide connection-level isolation for projects that should be unaware of each other, with explicit operational tradeoffs.
- [PostgreSQL CREATE DATABASE](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createdatabase.html>) - Database creation is a privileged provisioning operation and must not be granted to the ordinary runtime application role.
- [SQLite isolation](<https://sqlite.org/isolation.html>) - SQLite provides transactional isolation within a database file; separate host-derived files provide a physical placement boundary for local runtime instances.
- [W3C ARIA23 chat log technique](<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/aria/ARIA23>) - Supports an initially empty, sequentially updated chat history exposed with role=log.
- [NIST AI 600-1](<https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence>) - Supports explicit pre-deployment evaluation of capabilities, limits, risks, and deployment-context behavior.
- [OWASP LLM01 Prompt Injection](<https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/>) - Supports keeping authorization and privileged actions in application code instead of granting them to the model.

## High-level decisions

### Published chatbot interaction boundary

How should an exact published chatbot composition, its selected model, and the existing controlled conversation runtime be connected?

The choice determines whether the asset-driven system remains authoritative, whether existing approval and runtime controls are preserved, and how reusable the solution will be for future conversational systems.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `typed-composition-runtime-binding`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Typed composition runtime binding (typed-composition-runtime-binding) | Add an authorized text-model picker to the message-composer properties, carry the exact model record through validated composition/build/runtime evidence, and mount an interactive shared conversation controller over the published visual hierarchy while reusing existing session, approval, transcript, turn, guard, and Python adapter services. | yes | Largest coherent cross-layer change, but it closes the real composition-to-runtime gap instead of adding a second chatbot architecture.; Requires typed model-choice projection and release-to-reviewed-plan/session resolution across shared contracts and both hosts.; Keeps the asset hierarchy responsible for presentation while application services remain responsible for state and execution. | History begins empty and shows only persisted bounded transcript entries.; The composer is editable and Send invokes the configured approved model through the existing controlled path.; Future supported conversational templates can reuse the same typed runtime binding without bespoke screens.; Arbitrary asset code remains non-executable and unsupported features remain explicit. |
| Bespoke reference chatbot surface (bespoke-reference-chatbot-surface) | Detect the controlled-chatbot template at launch and replace its asset-rendered runtime with a purpose-built chat component wired to the existing conversation APIs and a separate model selector. | no | Smaller initial UI change and simpler local state.; Duplicates the visual composition and weakens the meaning of the built asset hierarchy.; Every future conversational template risks another template-specific runtime screen. | The reference chatbot could work sooner, but composer property changes would not fully define the running interface.; Preview and runtime behavior could diverge.; Template-specific branches would accumulate in shared Systems UI. |
| Executable asset backing resources (executable-asset-backing-resources) | Allow frontend and backend backing resources attached to assets to execute directly and implement conversation state, model calls, and rendering from those resources. | no | Offers maximum asset flexibility.; Introduces an unqualified arbitrary-code sandbox, capability, supply-chain, packaging, and host-isolation problem.; Would substantially broaden the accepted architecture and security scope. | The current trusted declarative runtime and controlled invocation boundary would no longer be sufficient.; A separate sandbox qualification roadmap and architecture decision would be required before production use.; This option cannot safely deliver the requested production-ready successor within the current constraints. |

### Published system runtime isolation

What physical window and database isolation topology should the approved interactive runtime use?

The desktop must launch a separate Electron window, and system-owned runtime data must not share a database with another installed system. The topology must keep privileged window, database, model, and execution authority in the host while preserving one shared application architecture.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `dedicated-runtime-data-plane`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dedicated runtime data plane (dedicated-runtime-data-plane) | Give every installed system runtime an opaque durable runtime-instance identity, a dedicated physical database, and—on desktop—a dedicated sandboxed BrowserWindow with a runtime-only preload and unique non-persistent browser session. Keep lifecycle, release, placement, and audit metadata in the platform control-plane database. Desktop uses one contained SQLite file per runtime instance; managed hosts use provisioner-created PostgreSQL databases with separate least-privilege runtime bindings. | yes | Strongest consistent cross-system data separation and cleanest runtime authority boundary.; Requires database placement/provisioning, per-instance migrations, connection lifecycle, backup/restore, quotas, and recovery.; Requires a second packaged Electron renderer/preload entry and exact sender-to-runtime-instance IPC binding.; Separates data-plane persistence from current shared control-plane repositories, so conversation and system-data composition must become runtime-instance scoped. | Start opens or focuses the exact system window automatically; no system runtime modal remains in the builder.; Stop closes the system window and active data resources without deleting durable data.; Compatible release upgrades can retain the same runtime instance and database through explicit migration; clones and separate installations receive new databases.; Uninstall retains the database until a separate explicit, confirmed data-deletion operation applies retention and backup policy.; A system renderer cannot choose paths, connection strings, runtime identities, model identities, or another system's IPC channels.; Desktop and managed hosts reuse the same runtime controller and application services while host adapters own Electron and database-specific mechanics. |
| Hybrid isolation (hybrid-desktop-dedicated-server-pooled) | Use a dedicated SQLite file and sandboxed BrowserWindow for each desktop runtime instance, but keep managed-server runtime data in the existing shared PostgreSQL database with organization, workspace, and system partition keys plus row-level security. | no | Delivers physical isolation on desktop with substantially less managed-database provisioning work.; Preserves existing pooled PostgreSQL operations and backup tooling.; Provides different isolation guarantees by deployment shape and does not satisfy physical database separation for managed systems. | Desktop systems cannot share a runtime database file.; Managed systems still depend on logical predicates and row-level security inside one database.; Cross-host conformance must describe two different data-isolation guarantees. |
| Logical isolation only (shared-database-logical-isolation) | Open each desktop system in a dedicated sandboxed BrowserWindow but continue storing all runtime data in the shared platform database under stricter organization, workspace, release, and system keys. | no | Smallest persistence change and lowest operational cost.; Relies on every repository query and policy layer to preserve cross-system isolation.; Does not create a system-specific database instance. | The window requirement is met but the requested physical data boundary is not.; A persistence-scoping defect could still expose records across systems.; This option is not recommended for the stated protection goal. |

## Increment 1: Release-bound conversation runtime and model selection

- Id: `release-bound-conversation-runtime`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Turn the controlled chatbot composition into a deterministic, release-bound interaction contract with an authorized model selected from the message-composer properties.

### Work packages

- **Typed interaction and model-binding contracts** (`runtime-contract`): Implementation-neutral contracts describe the interactive conversation surface, exact model resource binding, runtime-instance identity, lifecycle ownership, and sanitized failure semantics without allowing authored code or renderer-selected authority.
- **Authorized model selection in the Composer** (`composer-model-selection`): The message-composer properties expose a required dynamic picker containing only compatible, workspace-authorized text-generation models; stale, cross-workspace, unavailable, and incompatible references fail closed.
- **Deterministic build and release materialization** (`deterministic-runtime-materialization`): Revision validation, build locks, releases, and trusted launch descriptors preserve the exact model and interaction binding needed at runtime, with digests and non-sensitive diagnostics.
- **Connected reference-chat semantics** (`reference-chat-semantics`): The controlled chatbot reference template defines one linked history/composer interaction, starts with an empty runtime transcript, and retains inert sample-free behavior in design previews.

### Deliverables

- Typed interaction, model-binding, and runtime-instance contracts
- Dynamic authorized model-resource picker in shared Composer UI and both clients
- Revision validator and deterministic build/release propagation
- Updated controlled-chatbot foundation definitions and reference template
- Focused contract, validation, materialization, UI, and denial-path tests
- Affected architecture, ADR, context-pack, and nearest README updates

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authorized-model-picker`: The message-composer properties require selection from the current workspace's compatible, authorized text-generation models and never accept an arbitrary provider, path, or model identifier. | local | passed (test) |
| `model-binding-fails-closed`: Missing, stale, cross-workspace, incompatible, or unavailable model bindings block revision validation, build, release activation, or runtime start at the appropriate boundary with sanitized diagnostics. | local | passed (test) |
| `release-binding-is-deterministic`: Repeated builds of the same valid revision resolve the same interaction and model binding in the lock and release, while a changed binding changes the relevant digest. | local | passed (test) |
| `reference-chat-is-sample-free`: The controlled chatbot reference composition contains one connected history/composer interaction and its runtime contract does not seed example user or assistant messages. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-release-authority-reviewed`: Model authority remains owned by application and host services; forged renderer values, unauthorized resources, and diagnostic disclosure paths are denied and evidenced. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused contract, Composer-property, revision-validation, build-materialization, release-compatibility, and reference-template tests while implementing each work package.
- Run focused forged-reference, stale-resource, cross-workspace, unavailable-runtime, and sanitized-diagnostic denial tests.
- After all work packages are complete, run the applicable documentation, architecture, agent-support, desktop/thin-client build, and repository test gates once for the increment.

### Rollback

Remove the additive interaction/model-binding contract and picker before dependent releases are approved; releases that require the new contract remain fail-closed rather than silently falling back to an unbound model.

### Excluded

- Dedicated database provisioning and migration
- Electron runtime-window creation
- Arbitrary imported executable asset code
- New model-provider installation or credential-management flows

## Increment 2: Dedicated system runtime data plane

- Id: `dedicated-system-runtime-data-plane`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `release-bound-conversation-runtime`

Give every installed system runtime an opaque durable identity and a physically separate database while keeping lifecycle, placement, release, and audit metadata in the platform control plane.

### Work packages

- **Runtime-instance lifecycle and placement** (`runtime-instance-lifecycle`): Application ports and use cases allocate, resolve, migrate, stop, retain, and explicitly delete runtime instances without accepting renderer-supplied paths, connection strings, or identities.
- **Per-system desktop SQLite databases** (`desktop-runtime-database`): Each desktop runtime instance owns a contained host-derived SQLite file, runtime-scoped repositories, migrations, bounded connection lifetime, health checks, backup/restore metadata, and restart recovery.
- **Per-system managed PostgreSQL databases** (`managed-runtime-database`): A provisioner-owned adapter creates a dedicated PostgreSQL database and least-privilege runtime role per instance, while runtime code receives only the opaque binding it needs and cannot create databases or cross instance boundaries.
- **Runtime-scoped conversation and system data** (`conversation-data-cutover`): Conversation sessions, turns, messages, responses, execution records, and system-owned data are composed against the selected runtime database; shared control-plane storage retains only bounded placement and lifecycle references.

### Deliverables

- Runtime-instance, placement, retention, migration, and deletion contracts and use cases
- Control-plane runtime-instance repository
- Per-instance SQLite database factory and runtime repository composition
- PostgreSQL database provisioner and least-privilege runtime binding adapters
- Migration, recovery, backup/restore, quota, and connection-lifecycle controls
- Cross-instance isolation, lifecycle, failure-injection, SQLite, and live PostgreSQL qualification tests
- Persistence, host-model, security, deployment, and operations documentation

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `physical-database-isolation`: Two installed systems receive different physical databases and cannot enumerate, read, write, migrate, restore, or delete one another's data through public or adapter-level paths. | local | passed (test) |
| `desktop-runtime-data-survives-lifecycle`: Desktop conversation and system data survive stop, process restart, and compatible release upgrade; clone or separate installation receives a new database; uninstall retains data until a separate explicit confirmed deletion. | local | passed (test) |
| `managed-postgres-database-isolation`: Live PostgreSQL qualification proves that each runtime role is restricted to its provisioner-created database and cannot connect to or mutate another runtime database or perform provisioning operations. | controlled-environment | passed (test) |
| `runtime-data-recovery`: Migration failure, interrupted startup, connection exhaustion, backup, and restore paths fail safely and recover without substituting another system's database or corrupting control-plane state. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-runtime-data-plane-reviewed`: Opaque identity resolution, contained desktop paths, provisioner/runtime role separation, retention, deletion confirmation, redaction, quotas, and residual host-compromise risk are reviewed and evidenced. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused runtime-instance, repository, SQLite path-containment, lifecycle, migration, retention, backup/restore, and cross-instance denial tests while implementing each work package.
- Run the live PostgreSQL database-and-role isolation qualification against an explicitly configured disposable environment using synthetic data.
- After all work packages are complete, run the applicable documentation, architecture, security, server/desktop build, persistence conformance, and repository test gates once for the increment.

### Rollback

Disable new runtime-instance allocation and window start, preserve already-created databases and control-plane placement records, and require an explicit migration or deletion decision; never merge isolated runtime data back into the shared database automatically.

### Excluded

- Multi-region database replication
- Automatic destructive data deletion on uninstall
- Cross-system shared transcript storage
- Renderer-visible database paths or connection credentials

## Increment 3: Isolated interactive system window and production qualification

- Id: `isolated-interactive-system-window`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `dedicated-system-runtime-data-plane`

Launch the published controlled chatbot in a separate hardened Electron window whose usable composer invokes the selected model through the existing controlled conversation architecture and persists its real transcript in the system's dedicated database.

### Work packages

- **Dedicated hardened Electron runtime window** (`electron-runtime-window`): A main-process window manager creates or focuses one exact release/runtime-instance window using a dedicated renderer and minimal preload, unique non-persistent browser session, strict navigation and permission policy, exact sender binding, CSP, sandboxing, and bounded window resources.
- **Shared interactive conversation controller** (`interactive-chat-controller`): A host-neutral controller creates or resumes the release-bound approved conversation session, reads the real transcript, owns bounded draft and submit state, invokes the selected model through the controlled orchestration path, and persists one user/assistant result per successful turn.
- **Usable and accessible chatbot surface** (`usable-chat-surface`): The runtime window starts with empty history, permits typing, supports click and keyboard submission, disables duplicate sends, exposes progress and recoverable errors, renders only persisted messages, and keeps the builder window independent.
- **Lifecycle integration and production qualification** (`lifecycle-and-production-qualification`): Start opens or focuses the system window, Stop closes it and releases handles without deleting data, and packaged-desktop, Python text-generation, database, accessibility, performance, recovery, and reference-system end-to-end checks establish production readiness.

### Deliverables

- Second Electron Forge renderer/preload entry and runtime-window manager
- Runtime-only IPC contracts, authorization, sender binding, and lifecycle bridge
- Shared controlled-conversation runtime controller and interactive surface
- System Published lifecycle integration with no runtime modal
- Packaged desktop end-to-end and host-contract qualification fixtures
- Interaction, accessibility, navigation, IPC-forgery, resource-limit, persistence, restart, and failure-path tests
- End-user, architecture, security, packaging, troubleshooting, and operations documentation

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `system-opens-in-separate-window`: Starting a valid published visual system opens or focuses a separate Electron window bound to the exact runtime instance and release while the builder remains usable; the former runtime modal is not used. | controlled-environment | passed (test) |
| `chat-is-usable-and-persistent`: The controlled chatbot opens with no sample messages, accepts bounded text, submits by button and keyboard exactly once, invokes the configured authorized model, shows the persisted response, and reloads the same transcript after stop and restart. | controlled-environment | passed (test) |
| `conversation-controls-fail-safely`: Missing readiness, revoked approval, stale release/model binding, unavailable runtime, cancellation, timeout, and invocation failure produce recoverable sanitized UI states without duplicate turns, leaked protected context, or cross-system data access. | local | passed (test) |
| `runtime-window-is-hardened`: The runtime renderer has sandboxing and context isolation enabled, no Node integration, a minimal preload, strict CSP and permission/navigation denial, unique session isolation, exact sender-to-instance authorization, and bounded window/session creation. | local | passed (test) |
| `reference-runtime-production-qualified`: Packaged desktop, controlled Python text-generation, isolated database, accessibility, restart/recovery, and representative latency/resource tests pass for the reference controlled chatbot with synthetic non-sensitive fixtures. | controlled-environment | passed (test) |
| `security-runtime-window-reviewed`: Window, IPC, model, transcript, database, denial-of-service, redaction, rollback, and residual main-process/host-compromise risks are reviewed and evidenced before handoff. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused controller, renderer, accessibility, lifecycle, IPC authorization, navigation denial, duplicate-submit, cancellation, timeout, transcript, and resource-bound tests while implementing each work package.
- Compare the reference runtime's semantic rendered structure and interaction behavior with the approved sample-free chatbot fixture rather than brittle presentation-only snapshots.
- Run packaged Electron qualification with the controlled text-generation worker and isolated runtime database, then stop, restart, and verify transcript recovery.
- After all work packages are complete, run documentation, architecture, agent-support, security, server build, thin-client build, desktop package/build, and the full repository test suite once for the increment.

### Rollback

Disable runtime-window start and keep affected deployments stopped while preserving their isolated databases and audit state; do not restore the non-interactive modal or bypass controlled conversation execution.

### Excluded

- General execution of arbitrary authored or imported UI code
- A new unrestricted browser shell
- Provider credential entry inside the runtime window
- Cross-device realtime conversation synchronization
- Non-conversational reference-system interaction redesign
